title: 卜算子·送鲍浩然之浙东
titlePy: Bǔ Suàn Zǐ · Sòng Bào Hàorán Zhī Zhèdōng
titleEn: Song of the Diviner · Seeing Bao Haoran Off to Eastern Zhejiang
author: 王观
intro: A light-hearted farewell: the rivers of Zhejiang are a pretty woman’s glancing eyes, its hills her eyebrows — and if you catch up with spring there, the poet tells his friend, stay with it.
analysis: 这是一首送朋友去浙东的词，写得轻松俏皮，没有一般送别诗的眼泪。开头两句很新奇：江水像美人流动的眼波，青山像美人皱起的眉峰——把山水比作美人的眉眼，这种手法叫“比喻”，而且比得又活泼又美。接着问：朋友要去哪里？就是那山水像眉眼一样美丽的地方。下阕说：刚刚送走了春天，又要送你走，两件伤心事碰在一起。但词人没有沉在悲伤里，反而祝福朋友：如果你到了江南，还赶得上那里的春天，千万要和春天住在一起啊！“和春住”三个字把春天当成可以同住的朋友，既是祝福，也是不舍。全词语言像说话一样自然，比喻新巧，是宋词送别作品中很有个性的一首。
analysisEn: This is a farewell to a friend heading for eastern Zhejiang, and it is surprisingly cheerful — no tears, just affection and wit. The opening is unusual: the rivers there are a beautiful woman’s glancing eyes, the green hills her gathered eyebrows. Comparing a landscape to a lovely face is a metaphor, and here it is fresh and playful. Where is my friend going? To the place where hills and rivers look like a smiling face. The second stanza admits a double sadness: spring has only just left, and now the friend is leaving too. Instead of dwelling on it, the poet turns it into a wish: if you reach the south in time to catch spring there, be sure to stay with it. “Live together with spring” treats the season like a companion — a blessing and a goodbye at once. The language is as easy as conversation, which makes this one of the most charming farewell lyrics of the Song.
background: Wang Guan (dates uncertain, c. 1035–1100) passed the imperial examination in 1057 and served as an official; few details of his life survive. Bao Haoran was a friend from eastern Zhejiang returning home — nothing else is known about him.
pronunciation: 那边 nǎ biān（“那”同“哪”，旧时写作“那”）；盈盈 yíng yíng；和春住 hé。机器朗读“那边”会读成 nà，已在“朗读用字”列换成“哪边”，音频需人工听验。
version: 采用通行文本。“欲问行人去那边”一作“欲问行人去哪边”。

lines.lit: The water is a sideways glance of eyes;
lines.en: The rivers there are a woman’s glancing eyes,

lines.lit: the hills are eyebrow peaks drawn together.
lines.en: the hills, her eyebrows gently knit.

lines.py: yù wèn xíng rén qù nǎ biān
lines.lit: If you ask where the traveller is going —
lines.en: Where is my friend off to, you ask?

lines.lit: to the place where brows and eyes are lovely.
lines.en: To where those brows and eyes are smiling.

lines.lit: I have only just seen spring off;
lines.en: I have only just said goodbye to spring,

lines.lit: again I see you off on your way home.
lines.en: and now I am saying goodbye to you.

lines.py: ruò dào jiāng nán gǎn shàng chūn
lines.lit: If you reach Jiangnan and catch up with spring,
lines.en: If you get south in time to catch up with spring,

lines.lit: by all means live with spring.
lines.en: whatever you do, stay there with it.

words.note: 题目里的“之”是动词“去、往”，古义，今天不这样用。

words.en: the glance of the eyes, flowing like waves
words.note: 形容女子眼神流动，书面语仍用。
把眉毛比作山峰，现代汉语较少用。
眉峰聚：皱眉。现代汉语说“皱眉”。
古义指出远门的人；今天“行人”指路上走的人。
这里同“哪边”，古代“那”“哪”不分。

words.en: by all means; be sure to
words.note: 现代汉语仍这样用，如“千万别忘了”。

imagery.name: 水
imagery.zh: 江水被比作美人流动的眼波，写出浙东山水的灵动秀美。
imagery.en: The rivers become a beauty’s glancing eyes — lively, bright and inviting.

imagery.name: 山
imagery.zh: 青山被比作美人的眉峰，和眼波一起组成一张美丽的脸。
imagery.en: The hills become her eyebrows; with the rivers they form a lovely face of a landscape.

imagery.name: 春
imagery.zh: 春天刚走又送朋友，春天成了可以“同住”的伙伴，寄托对朋友的美好祝愿。
imagery.en: Spring has just left, and the friend is leaving too; spring becomes a companion to “live with” — a warm wish for him.
